title: A 100-ms acceleration time-arrow feature fails cross-placement stair-direction prediction, with a lag-dependent exploratory signal
abstract: A signed100-ms increment-asymmetry feature modestly improved subject-held-out WISDM stair-direction Brier loss (gain0.002143) but worsened a frozen model in independent waist-phone UCI HAR data (0.218936 to0.231522;gain-0.012586;400source-target participant-refit95% interval[-0.034424,0.000574]). A prespecified200-ms sensitivity improved target loss, but its uncertainty was quantified post-result and requires a third untouched cohort. This is lag- and model-dependent activity-state information,not a validated clinical marker.
